page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-32-lssd is a memory-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 248.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.75 GB of RAM per core, alongside a massive 504 MB L3 cache. Storage is bundled directly with the instance, consisting of five local NVMe SSDs totaling 1745 GB of local storage capacity. No dedicated GPU hardware is included in this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2307.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 36.83 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is also strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 18257.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 53228.41. In memory-intensive tasks, the server achieved a Passmark memory score of 2796.01 and a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 2702.38 GB/sec. However, large block memory write bandwidth is relatively lower at 77.81 GB/sec. For AI workloads, the hardware-assisted Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) support prompt processing speeds of 2648.07 tokens/sec for small LLM models, though text generation speeds drop to 2.83 tokens/sec for large 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-32-lssd offers a high density of memory and local NVMe storage relative to its 32 vCPUs, reducing the need to provision larger, more expensive instances solely for storage or RAM capacity. The inclusion of five local SSDs provides high-speed local scratch space without additional block storage attachment costs. This resource profile is suitable for memory-intensive databases, medium-scale data processing, local caching layers, and text-processing pipelines that benefit from high single-core CPU performance and fast local NVMe storage.
